description: Stage S3 axis-primacy calibration. Tags each of the 36 O7 atomic concept-axes as PRIMARY (a core product characteristic an exporter reliably knows AND that genuinely splits the tariff line) or INCIDENTAL (special-variant / niche flags an exporter may not know or that rarely discriminate the real product). The refined ASK rule keys off this: ASK on an unpinned PRIMARY axis that splits the survivors EVEN when the subheading carries a residual leaf; DEFAULT to the residual (do NOT ask) when only INCIDENTAL axes are unresolved. CONSERVATIVE BY CONSTRUCTION: when unsure, an axis is marked INCIDENTAL (over-asking is the catastrophic failure). Justifications are one line each. Loaded read-only by lib/askable-surface-table.ts; the build artifact askable-surface.json folds these tags into per-axis is_primary flags.

legend.PRIMARY: Core characteristic an exporter reliably knows and that splits the line — askable even over a residual.
legend.INCIDENTAL: Special-variant / niche / hard-to-self-assess flag — default to residual, do not ask.

axes.justification: Fresh/chilled vs frozen vs live is a top-of-mind shipment fact every food/seafood exporter states up front.
Whole carcass vs cuts vs offal is the exporter's own product description and is the canonical frozen-chicken split.
Roasted vs green coffee/cocoa is a defining, obvious product state the exporter always knows.
Decaffeinated vs regular is a clear yes/no the seller knows; it splits coffee/tea lines into distinct codes.
Plantation/Cherry/Parchment (and the Arabica-vs-Robusta species it encodes) is core coffee-trade vocabulary the grower/exporter knows.
Dry (natural) vs wet (washed) processing is standard coffee-export terminology stated on every lot.
A/B/C/AB/PB grade is the exporter's own sale grade printed on the contract; genuinely splits the leaf.
Unbleached/bleached/dyed/printed/yarn-dyed is the fabric's own finish state a textile exporter always specifies.
Plain/twill/dobby/damask weave is on the fabric spec sheet and discriminates the tariff leaf.
Cotton vs silk vs wool vs man-made fibre is the most basic textile fact and a hard tariff split.
PE/PP/PVC/PS polymer identity is on the plastic resin/article datasheet the exporter ships against.
Powder/liquid/solid/sheet/bar/tube is observable and stated; splits many chemical and material lines.
Hot-rolled/cold-rolled/drawn/cast/forged is core steel-trade vocabulary on every mill cert.
Galvanized/coated/uncoated is an obvious surface state the steel exporter always declares.
Seamless vs welded is the defining pipe attribute the manufacturer knows and that splits the leaf.
Complete machine vs part vs accessory is a fundamental distinction the exporter knows and that drives the code.
Motor vs generator is an unambiguous function the exporter states; clean two-way tariff split.
Bus/van/car/special-purpose is the vehicle's own identity, obvious to the exporter.
Worked vs unworked (and sorted vs unsorted) is a clear processing state the exporter declares for stones/skins/etc.
Natural vs synthetic vs reconstructed is a defining material origin the exporter always knows.
In-coils vs not-in-coils is a packing/delivery form many sellers omit and that is often implicit; conservative -> incidental.
Cellular vs non-cellular / rigid vs flexible is a technical foam/plastic sub-property a non-expert exporter may not self-assess reliably.
Aromatic/saturated/halogenated is chemist-level structural detail outside a general exporter's vocabulary; conservative -> incidental.
GSM band is a numeric spec sellers often do not have to hand at classify time; conservative -> incidental (numeric band).
Handloom vs mill is an India-specific special-variant flag; unflagged defaults to the mill leaf (unmarked-default-wins).
Embroidered / zari-border / chikan is a special-variant decoration; unflagged defaults to the plain residual leaf.
Retail vs bulk packing is a presentation flag that rarely the defining product fact; default to residual.
Industrial vs jewellery quality is a grading judgement a non-expert exporter may not self-assess; conservative -> incidental.
Air-conditioned vs not is a vehicle sub-feature; secondary to the vehicle-type fork and often a residual-bearing split.
Monocoque vs body-on-chassis is engineering detail a trader rarely knows; conservative -> incidental.
Seating-capacity band is a numeric threshold sellers may not map to the exact tariff band; conservative -> incidental (numeric band).
Power/output kW band is a numeric threshold the exporter may not align to tariff cut-offs; conservative -> incidental (numeric band).
kVA capacity band is a numeric threshold prone to mis-mapping to tariff cut-offs; conservative -> incidental (numeric band).
Outer-diameter band is a numeric measurement seldom stated as a tariff band; conservative -> incidental (numeric band).
Container-size band is a numeric capacity threshold the seller may not align to tariff cut-offs; conservative -> incidental (numeric band).
Intended end-use (apparel/household/industrial...) is interpretive, often dual-use, and frequently the residual-default axis; conservative -> incidental.
